en: The Sūtra on the Timely and the Untimely Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing of India.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha in the Kalandakanivāpa Bamboo Grove.
At the Ārāma-vihāra, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"I shall expound for you the Sūtra on the Timely and the Untimely; listen well and reflect upon it!"
The bhikṣus said:
“So be it, World-Honored One!
We shall receive your instruction and listen.”
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"In this matter, what constitutes the proper time and what constitutes the improper time?"
“Bhikṣus, you should know:

during the first period of winter, from the sixteenth day of the eighth month to the thirtieth day, the first fifteen days constitute seven ‘quarters’ as the proper time (*kāla*), while four and a half quarters constitute the improper time (*akāla*).”
"On the twenty-fifth day, eight *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while six *pada*s and eight *aṅgula*s constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the first day to the fifteenth day of the ninth month."
"In the thirty-fifth day, nine *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while seven *pada*s and six *aṅgula*s constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the ninth month."
"On the forty-fifth day, ten *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while eight *pada*s and three *aṅgula*s constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the tenth month."
"On the fifty-fifth day, eleven *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while nine *pada*s and four finger-breadths constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the tenth month."
"On the sixty-fifth day, twelve *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while eleven *pada*s and six fingers constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the first to the fifteenth day of the eleventh month."
"On the seventy-fifth day, eleven quarters and a half of a foot constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while ten quarters and three finger-breadths constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth day of the eleventh month to the thirtieth day."
"On the eighty-fifth day, eleven *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while nine *pādas* and four finger-breadths (*aṅgula*) constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the twelfth month."
"At the beginning of spring, during the first fifteen days, ten *pada* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while eight *pada* minus three fingers is the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the sixteenth day of the twelfth month until the thirtieth day."
"On the twenty-fifth day, nine and a half *pada*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while seven *pada*s minus three finger-breadths constitutes the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the first day of the first month until the fifteenth day."
"On the thirty-fifth day, nine *pada* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while six *pada* minus three fingers constitutes the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the first month."
"On the forty-fifth day, eight *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while five *pādas* minus three fingers constitutes the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the first to the fifteenth day of the second month."
"On the fifty-fifth day, seven *pāda*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*); three *pāda*s less three fingers constitutes the improper time (*akāla*).
This refers to the period from the sixteenth day of the second month to the thirtieth day."
"On the sixty-fifth day, six *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while three *pādas* less four fingers constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the third month."
"On the seventy-fifth day, five *pāda*s constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while three *pāda*s minus three fingers constitutes the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the third month."
"On the eighty-fifth day, four *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while two *pādas* minus one finger-breadth is not the proper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the fourth month."

In the first half of summer, from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the fourth month: the first fifteen days constitute the "proper time" (*kāla*), during which three quarters of the day remain; the remaining four quarters of a finger-breadth constitute the "improper time" (*akāla*).
The period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the fourth month is as follows.
"On the twenty-fifth day, two feet constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while one foot minus five finger-breadths constitutes the improper time (*akāla*);
this applies from the first day to the fifteenth day of the fifth month."
"In the thirty-fifth day, two and a half feet constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while one foot less three finger-breadths is the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth to the thirtieth day of the fifth month."
"In the forty-fifth day, three and a half *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), while two *pādas* minus two finger-breadths constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the sixth month."
"On the fifty-fifth day, four and a half *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), and two and a half *pādas* constitute the improper time (*akāla*);
this refers to the period from the sixteenth day of the sixth month to the thirtieth day."
"On the sixty-fifth day, five *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*) and three *pādas* constitute the improper time (*akāla*).
This refers to the period from the first to the fifteenth day of the seventh month.
On the seventy-fifth day, five and a half *pādas* constitute the proper time and three and a half *pādas* constitute the improper time."
“From the sixteenth day of the seventh month to the thirtieth day.
On the eighty-fifth day, six *pādas* constitute the proper time (*kāla*), and four and a half *pādas* constitute the improper time (*akāla*).
From the first day of the eighth month to the fifteenth day.”
"In this way, monks!

I have already explained the twelve months as being either the proper time or the improper time for the conduct that should be practiced by the śrāvakas; I have spoken thus out of compassion and for their benefit."
"What I was to do has been completed; you should now go forth.
Whether beneath a tree, in an empty place, or sitting in the open air, engage in contemplation.
O bhikṣus!"
"Do not be negligent, lest you later fall into regret; this is my instruction and admonition.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, all the bhikṣus were filled with great joy, and they encouraged one another to receive and uphold it.
"Because of the causal condition of contempt, one falls into hell at the end of life;
because of the causal condition of cultivating goodness, one is reborn in heaven in this life.
By virtue of cultivating wholesome karma through these conditions, one leaves evil behind and attains liberation."
"Due to the causes and conditions of unwholesome desire, one enters the evil realms when the body perishes.
Thus spoke the Indian Tripiṭaka Master Jayasena, who, holding the Sanskrit manuscript in his hand, translated it orally himself.
Copied in the city of Khotan by a monk from Liangzhou.
Clad in coarse cloth yet harboring a gem within; With profound wisdom appearing as a fool.
Outwardly like a barbarian, inwardly he cherishes a bright pearl; For billions of kalpas, he shall be one in essence with the Way.
Thus [he spoke].
